# What Stan cost us

## The integral solver would not hold

:::: {.columns}
::: {.column width="50%"}
```
Chain 252 Exception: Error in function
tanh_sinh<double>::integrate: The tanh_sinh
quadrature evaluated your function at a singular
point and got -0.038716888888388652. Integration
bounds were automatically narrowed, but the
integral was found to be increasing at the new
endpoint. ...

Warning: 243 chain(s) finished unexpectedly!
```

- **243 of 256** chains, dying after warmup rather than at
  initialisation
- `integrate_1d` errors rather than rejecting, and there is no
  `try`/`catch` to wrap it in
:::
::: {.column width="50%"}
```stan
// before
result = integrate_1d(
  primary_censored_integrand, lower_bound, d,
  theta, {d, pwindow}, ids, 1e-2
);

// after
result = ode_rk45(
  primary_censored_ode, y0, lower_bound, {d},
  theta, {d, pwindow}, ids
)[1, 1];
```

- Recast as an ODE, **0 of 600**
:::
::::

::: {.attribution}
epinowcast/primarycensored#34 and PR #64, commit `1c4e6f1`, September
2024. Nine days from opening the issue to merging the ODE recast. Also
reported four to five times faster, from one run rather than a
benchmark.
:::

## Everything I tried in between

![](../figures/delays-stan-failures.png){width="80%"
fig-align="center"
fig-alt="Horizontal bar chart of ten runs reported in
epinowcast/primarycensored issue 34. The first, integrate_1d at
tolerance 1e-6, lost 243 of 256 chains. Eight tuning attempts sit
between 12 and 27 per cent, one of them a model with the truncation
adjustment removed. The last, recast as ode_rk45, lost 0 of 600."}

::: {.attribution}
Every run is one Sam Abbott reported in
[epinowcast/primarycensored#34][pc-issue34] between 5 and 12 September
2024, read back from the issue, `scripts/delays-stan-failures.py`. The
runs are not one dataset. The scenario was made harder in the same PR
that landed the ODE, so the last two rows on 600 chains are the pair
closest to like for like.
:::

[pc-issue34]: https://github.com/epinowcast/primarycensored/issues/34

## No user types, so distributions became integers

:::: {.columns}
::: {.column width="44%"}
| id | R, `pcd_distributions` | Stan, `dist_lcdf` | |
|---:|---|---|---|
| 1 | `lnorm` | `lognormal` | ✓ |
| 2 | `gamma` | `gamma` | ✓ |
| 3 | **`weibull`** | **`normal`** | ✗ |
| 4 | `exp` | `exponential` | ✓ |
| 5 | `gengamma` | `weibull` | ✗ |
| 6 | `nbinom` | `beta` | ✗ |
| ... | | | |
| 17 | `logis` | `von_mises` | ✗ |

::: {.attribution}
Both tables as they stood at `4aaf249^`,
`data-raw/distributions.R:1-19` and
`inst/stan/functions/primarycensored_ode.stan:28-44`
:::
:::
::: {.column width="56%"}
```r
dist_id <- pcd_stan_dist_id(family_name)

stanvars_functions[[1]]$scode <- gsub(
  "dist_id", dist_id,
  stanvars_functions[[1]]$scode,
  fixed = TRUE
)
```

- The type parameter is an integer, pushed into Stan source as text,
  from another language, before the model compiles
- Ask for a Weibull on the numerical path and you fitted a normal. No
  error, no warning, numbers came back
- The fix came with a **228 line test** whose only job is checking that
  two integer tables agree

::: {.attribution}
`epidist/R/marginal_model.R:339-347` · fix in
epinowcast/primarycensored#277, commit `4aaf249`, February 2026
:::
:::
::::

::: {.callout-important}
`primary_censored(Weibull(2, 1), Uniform(0, 1))` carries the type. There
is no second table for it to disagree with.
:::
